name: Continuous identity governance across the employment lifecycle

attribution.legal_posture: Peer-reviewed defensive governance analysis; person-level attribution and control effectiveness require separate evidence.

caveats: Behavioral biometrics, location telemetry, digital-footprint review, or unexpected live checks can be intrusive and error-prone; use only where lawful and proportionate, with minimization, human review, accessibility accommodations, and appeal paths.
Multi-factor authentication remains valuable; the bounded point is that it may be insufficient when an adversary controls the enrolled endpoint or uses a facilitator.
The article provides governance analysis rather than a controlled effectiveness study of DPRK-specific interventions.

statements: Use this source-qualified context for governance or corroborated behavior-based review, never as standalone identity or nationality attribution.
limitations: No single nationality, geography, language, education history, technical skill, remote-work preference, interview anomaly, authentication event, or device signal establishes fraud or DPRK attribution.

statements: Peer-reviewed policy research frames remote-employment fraud as an identity-governance problem spanning recruitment, authentication, authorization, monitoring, and offboarding, and recommends recurring, contextual verification alongside least privilege and segmentation.
limitations: The article provides governance analysis rather than a controlled effectiveness study of DPRK-specific interventions.
